chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding what Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took from the allegiances upon the women is that they would not be sitting with their knees up, nor would be sitting with the men in private.
ai.seo_question: What behavioral restrictions did women pledge to the Prophet Muhammad regarding their posture and sitting with men?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific behavioral stipulations included in the covenant of allegiance (bay'ah) taken by women from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as narrated through the chain of the Twelve Imams' companions. It highlights the prohibition of 'ihtibān'—interpreted by Shia scholars as raising the knees or a specific posture of modesty—and restricting women from sitting with men in private areas (khala'ah), thereby reinforcing social boundaries and gender segregation in early Islamic practice.
